newsitem.title: JAPAN: Naphtha origin, quality discussed at Tokyo meeting.
newsitem.headline: Naphtha origin, quality discussed at Tokyo meeting.

text.p: Oil product traders at an open-spec naphtha conference in Tokyo discussed expanding the origin of cargoes traded under the contract to include Indonesian heavy condensate, participants said on Monday.
Trading house naphtha traders want to expand the origins of open-spec naphtha cargoes to allow heavy condensate from Indonesia.

Traders at petrochemical firms, however, were cautious of the proposal, saying stringent quality standards should be applied if Indonesian heavy condensate were to be traded as open-spec naphtha, conference participants said.
The two-day meeting ends on Tuesday.
South Korea's possible participation as a supplier instead of a buyer of open-spec cargoes will be discussed on Tuesday, traders said.
Open-spec naphtha is currently traded on a C and F (cost and freight) Japan or South Korea basis, restricting the two east Asian countries to buyers of open-spec cargoes.

However, some South Korean oil firms are seeking to take part in Asia's benchmark forward contract trading as cargo suppliers rather than importers as the country's refining capacity expands, traders said.
